data.why: The repository ships three ready-to-use datasets with pre-computed embeddings (data/cytometry_2500, data/german_socio_eco, data/ImmuneW_HDdata) and the app loads cytometry_2500 by default; no external or synthetic data is needed.

goals: Load a bundled dataset and view its hierarchical clustering dendrogram alongside a 2D embedding
Tune clustering parameters (alpha, beta, min/max explanatory attributes) and observe how the clusters and their explanations change
Inspect which attributes best explain why each cluster formed, ranked by explanatory strength
Switch between datasets (e.g. flow cytometry markers vs. socio-economic indicators) to compare clustering structure across domains
Import a custom dataset or a pre-computed embedding via the sidebar upload controls and explore it the same way

review.summary: The tree captures what the tool is for: cluster on an embedding, then read ranked per-attribute KDE explanations for computed clusters and for regions you select. The screens I checked all back it up, and the depth and features are mostly well judged. The KDE legend is described wrongly in both the task and the feature, and the import paths (dataset, embedding, labels) and the clustering's embedding setting are missing or misplaced, so it needs those fixes before filing.
